overall: Atlanta is having a drier-than-typical June afternoon with low dewpoints (~52°F) and mostly clear skies (FEW, 12% cloud cover). Temperatures peaked at 82.4°F around 13:19 ET and have been essentially flat for nearly two hours, running well below the NWS forecast high of 87°F. The overall pattern is cooler than the official forecast suggested, with high pressure keeping conditions stable but limiting the afternoon heating surge.
forecast_obs_notes: There is notable disagreement between the NWS text forecast (87°F) and the NWP model suite — ECMWF (80.7°F) and NBM (80.6°F) are actually below the current observed running max of 82.4°F, while HRRR (83.1°F) is closest to observed reality. The NWS narrative appears to be a significant overforecast relative to both model guidance and current observations. NWP timing models still suggest a peak around 16–17h ET, but the intraday obs-driven model places the peak at 14.7h, consistent with the temperature plateau already observed.
max_temp_prediction: With the running max locked at 82.4°F for nearly two hours and near-zero 30-minute velocity, further meaningful warming is unlikely. There is a small possibility of a marginal late-afternoon nudge given NWP peak timing around 16–17h ET and the 2-hour velocity still showing +0.9°F/hr in the broader trend, but the intraday model strongly favors the 82–83°F bucket (52.6%) with secondary support for 84–85°F (35.3%). Confidence is moderate-high that today's TMAX lands in the 82–84°F range, most likely near 83.5°F, well short of the NWS 87°F forecast.
